extracted.intended_audience: researchers invited to peer review for F1000Research (invited reviewers and potential co-reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for invited peer reviewers on F1000Research’s open, post-publication peer review model, including who may review, how to assess articles, required disclosures, and how to write and submit a review. Focused on producing constructive, reproducible, and transparent review reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, transparent post-publication review model
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research operates a fully open and transparent post-publication peer review process: reviewing happens after an article has been published openly on the platform, and peer reviews (including reviewer name and affiliation) are published alongside the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect their full report, name and affiliation to be made public and assigned a DOI. Editorial staff will invite reviewers and will check submitted reports against quality criteria and the Code of Conduct before publication. Be prepared for your report to be read and cited by the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess quality and validity (ignore novelty/interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to assess the quality and validity of the research, ignoring the novelty or perceived interest of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether the study is academically sound rather than whether results are 'exciting'. Null and negative studies are welcome and should be judged by the same standards as positive studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select approval status
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with the full report, reviewers must select an approval status for the research: Approved, Approved with reservations, or Not approved, and answer the Peer Review Questions for that article type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the approval status that best reflects your evaluation of the article’s validity and quality; use the Peer Review Questions to justify and explain the selection in your report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified reviewer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You should hold a doctorate (PhD/MD/MBBS or equivalent) to review for F1000Research; in fields where these are less common, other factors such as publication history or industry experience may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack a doctorate but have relevant experience or publication record, disclose this when invited and justify suitability to the Editorial team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrable expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: You should have demonstrable experience within the same field as the submitted article; for some subject areas this can mean being lead author on three publications in the last five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When expertise cannot be measured by publication history, provide other explanations of suitability (relevant technical experience, specific methodological expertise). If unsure, check the abstract and discuss with Editorial staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and competing interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must be impartial and must disclose any competing interests (financial or non-financial) that could impact their assessment to the Editorial team before accepting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of competing interests include: having published with any of the lead authors in the last 3 years, being part of the same institute as any author, or being a close collaborator. Raise any potential competing interests with Editorial staff before accepting the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional and geographic diversity of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure validity of the process, reviewers of the same article are required to be from different institutions and authors are encouraged to suggest reviewers from different countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect editors to select reviewers from different institutions and, where possible, diverse countries to provide varied perspectives on the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the article in full (including figures, tables, and data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read the article in full before writing their report, including viewing associated figures, tables, and the underlying data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not form conclusions from the abstract alone. Check figures, tables and available source data to verify results and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed, referenced feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Include as much detail as possible (with references, as needed) so that authors can fully understand what needs changing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete, specific examples and cite literature when recommending methodological or interpretive changes. Vague comments are less helpful for authors seeking to improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify priority of requested changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify which points in your review are most important for the authors to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between major issues that must be resolved and minor suggestions or stylistic improvements to help authors prioritize revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be critical but constructive (tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any concerns or criticisms of the article, but keep the tone constructive: the review should help the authors improve their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques to enable improvement; avoid hostile or dismissive language. Balance negative findings with guidance on how to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring in a co-reviewer when outside expertise is needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider bringing in a co-reviewer if any areas of the article are beyond your expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-reviewers (often ECRs or method specialists) can be credited openly; add co-reviewer names when submitting so they receive recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with COPE and the F1000Research Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to comply with the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and F1000Research’s Code of Conduct when writing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial staff will check reports against these standards prior to publication. Failure to comply may prevent publication of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure reviews for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure your review with headings and numbered lists to make it easy to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear headings (e.g., Major concerns, Minor issues, Methods, Statistics) and numbered points so authors and readers can quickly identify and act on specific feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and citation of current literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the work clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for clear writing, logical flow, and appropriate, up-to-date references. Flag missing key literature and suggest specific citations where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of study design and academic merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the study design appropriate and does the work have academic merit?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the chosen methods address the research question, whether controls and sampling are adequate, and whether the study advances knowledge or is methodologically sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of methods and analysis for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Are sufficient details of methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure materials, protocols, software, and analysis pipelines are described or linked; request additional methodological detail where necessary to enable reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of statistical analysis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check statistical methods, justification for tests used, treatment of multiple comparisons, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and whether interpretations are supported by the analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of source data for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that underlying datasets, code, and materials are accessible or suitably archived; request data sharing or clearer links where absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of conclusions by results
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure interpretations and conclusions do not overreach the presented data; ask authors to temper claims or provide additional analysis if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare any competing interests within the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any conflicting or competing interests must be disclosed, to maintain the integrity of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state any relevant competing interests when submitting the review. Failing to declare COI undermines transparency and may require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission procedure and use online form
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your report using the online form linked in the invitation or via the Peer Reviewing page; you can save a draft, preview and then submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot submit via the online form, request a peer review form from Editorial and return it by email. After submission (unless issues arise), the review will be published alongside the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewing recognition and submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When co-reviewing, invited reviewers should include co-reviewer names on submission so co-reviewers receive open credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1000Research encourages co-reviewing as training for ECRs; co-reviewers’ names and affiliations are published with the review and receive recognition (DOI, ORCID, Publons).
